13/09/2014

Admitting Officer

Emergency Department

Newtown Hospital

Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Ms Sally McConville, aged 38 years old

I am writing this letter to refer you Ms McConville, a 38-year-old administrator, whose features are
suggestive of acute asthma or a possible pneumonia. Your urgent management and investigations would
be highly appreciated.

Regarding her social and medical history, she is a non-smoker and she has a medical history of asthma for
which she has been managed accordingly.

On 10/09/2014, she came with a complaint of a productive cough with a yellow sputum, fever, wheezes
and a 2-day history of a runny nose. On examination, she had a red throat associated with scattered
wheezes. Thus, she was given Ventolin. Two days later, she came back with an increased shortness of
breath particularly with any minimal exertion and wheezes in the last 24 hours associated with fever and a     Commented [jc1]: ,
yellow sputum. Upon examination, she had a red throat as well as mildly elevated work of breathing and
widespread wheezes with no crepitations. Therefore, she was commenced on Amoxicillin and prednisolone
with continuity of her own medication.

Today, she attended my surgery complaining of fever and a worsening shortness of breath, despite her
medication. Upon examination, she had shortness of breath at rest as well as increased work of breathing
and accessory muscle use. Moreover, her hest chest examination showed a widespread wheezes and a
bibasal crepitations. In addition, her both respiratory rate and pulse rate were elevated. Furthermore, her    Commented [jc2]: both her
blood pressure was low. Thus, she was given salbutamol. However, no improvement was noticed and she is
still in respiratory distress.

In light of the above, your assessment is required promptly. If you have any queries, please do not hesitate
to contact me.

Yours faithfully,

Doctor
